title: Add independent quality judge substrate for non-deterministic loop standards

output.summary: Approve independent judge substrate for non-deterministic quality standards.

approvedRows.question: DTR-independent-quality-judge
approvedRows.currentState: Production loop standards have explicit method ownership and runner wiring, but non-deterministic standards are not independently judged or cacheable.
approvedRows.desiredState: Add an optional independent quality judge substrate for agent_self_assessment and model_judge standards with fake-judge tests, batching, caching, and deterministic hard-gate skip behavior.
approvedRows.rationale: False pass is the highest-cost error; non-deterministic standards need independent review without making deterministic gates depend on a model service.
approvedRows.userImpact: Future loop attempts can get stronger semantic QA without slowing deterministic failure paths.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers get a testable judge interface and cache contract before plugging in a real worker.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Small bounded runner substrate with direct fake-worker tests and no public UX change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Eligible non-deterministic standards are sent to at most one batched judge call per loop attempt.
Judge verdicts are cacheable by graph hash, prompt version, and input/evidence hash.
Deterministic hard-gate failures skip judge calls and deterministic gates do not require a model dependency.

approvedRows.recommendationRationale: The substrate is optional, covered by fake tests, and preserves current behavior when no judge is supplied.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: The user explicitly asked to continue with independent non-deterministic worker/model-judge checks.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Completes the next runner architecture slice without introducing external model requirements.
agentAssessment.rationale: Optional judge hooks provide independent review while keeping deterministic quality standards authoritative.

approvedRows.currentPain: Agent self-assessment standards can pass based only on submitted fields and no independent worker verdict exists.
approvedRows.desiredOutcome: Runner attempts can inject a judge worker that reviews eligible non-deterministic standards once per attempt and records compact judge metadata.
approvedRows.successSignal: Tests prove one batched judge call, judge failure affecting standards, cache hits by graph/prompt/input-evidence hash, and no judge call after deterministic hard-gate failure.
nonGoals: Do not add a real model provider dependency.
Do not make judge service required for deterministic gates.
Do not add public tool names.

acceptanceEvidenceItems.summary: runLoopQualityGraphEvaluation batches eligible agent_self_assessment/model_judge standards into one judge call per attempt, proven by fake judge tests.
Judge requests use graph hash, prompt version, and input/evidence hash cache keys with MemoryLoopQualityJudgeCache test coverage.
Deterministic hard-gate failure skips judge calls; without a supplied judge deterministic execution remains unchanged.

implementationAssessment.maintainability: Judge contracts live in src/loops/judge.ts and evaluator integration is isolated to runner-backed quality evaluation.
implementationAssessment.simplicity: No real model provider or global dependency was added; judge workers are injected through runner options.
implementationAssessment.projectStyle: Matches method ownership, false-pass risk, and hard-gate policies documented for loop quality graphs.
implementationAssessment.errorHandling: Judge worker errors become blocking judge verdicts; missing verdicts block the affected standard.
implementationAssessment.uncertaintyResolution: Typecheck, targeted tests, full tests, build, lab reports, audit, and diff hygiene passed.
implementationAssessment.rationale: This adds the independent-worker substrate while preserving normal deterministic loop execution.

sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.security: No network, auth, secret, permission, or provider integration was added.
sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.privacy: Judge input is caller-supplied and no external service is invoked by default.
sensitiveSurfaceAssessment.rationale: The implementation is optional local interfaces, cache helpers, docs, and tests.
